summary.title: Ball
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add a movable, bouncing ball object to a 2D Breakout-style OpenGL game, stick it to the paddle, and launch it with the space bar.
takeaways: Create a BallObject class derived from GameObject with a radius and a Stuck flag.
Move the ball each frame by adding velocity times delta time, and reverse velocity when it hits the left, right, or top edge.
Keep the ball attached to the paddle while it is stuck, and release it when the space bar is pressed.
Brick collision detection is the next step and is not implemented on this page.
summary.summary: This LearnOpenGL page continues a 2D Breakout-style game built with modern OpenGL. It introduces a BallObject class that extends GameObject with a radius, a Stuck flag, and a Move function that updates position and bounces the ball off the window's left, right, and top edges. The author adds the ball in Game::Init, updates it in Game::Update, handles space bar input to free it from the paddle, and renders it. The page ends by noting that the ball does not yet collide with bricks, which is the topic of the next step.
